text:
sam: FYI incident this morning — customer reported an api_key that was revoked still authorizing requests for ~45s. They saw a config change happen after revoke and some calls still went through.

kim: that's the cache TTL problem again. edge caches + internal policy caches had a 60s TTL. revoke paths were async and only invalidated local cache on write.

jordyn: details: revoke API returned 200 immediately, primary auth store updated, but edge nodes pull revocation snapshot on 60s tick. one node missed immediate resync due to transient DB read error and kept serving.

lee: sad. we need a deterministic revocation propagation design. today we have two mechanisms: 1) snapshot polling (60s) and 2) per-node invalidation via async fanout on write (best-effort). Both have gaps.

sam: proposal: introduce revocation sequence numbers + signed revocation deltas. core idea: each update increments a monotonic rev_seq. nodes keep highest seq seen. When validating token/key, node checks token.rev_seen >= key.rev_seq or queries a small proof endpoint if mismatch.

kim: interesting. so on revoke we publish small signed delta {rev_seq:123, key_id: "K", op: "revoke"} signed by revocation issuer key. nodes can apply deltas immediately. For nodes that missed deltas (e.g., restart), they fetch snapshot from seq N+1 onward.

jordyn: signing d/s is important for private deployments where operators may want to audit chain. Use HSM-signed deltas or at least service-signed with KMS. Also include ttl and expiry window.

lee: we also need a low-latency proof-lookup endpoint: /auth/v1/revocation_proof?key=K which returns {rev_seq:123, status:"revoked", sig:"..."}. Validator can call this synchronously if it sees a token with newer rev_seq than cached. But sync call for every missed rev would be expensive.

kim: optimize: validator only calls proof endpoint on cache miss or if token has explicit claim rev_seq > cached_seq. Normal flow uses local cache. For high-throughput edges, we can add a fast push channel (gRPC stream) from control plane -> edge cluster to deliver deltas. That reduces reliance on polling.

sam: Dedicated and Private differences: Hosted control plane can push deltas. Private installs might be air-gapped. For those we offer two modes: push via optional broker or signed snapshot artifacts that operators pull from an internal S3 on their schedule. We must ensure signed deltas work in both models.

jordyn: revoke/restore race: if a key is revoked then quickly restored, sequence numbers handle it. But we must ensure idempotency and tombstones with expiry so caches don't re-accept an older restore. Use monotonic seq and accept ops strictly by seq ordering.

lee: edge-case: token reuse where token itself contains last_seen_rev_seq claim. We should avoid relying on client-supplied rev metadata unless it's verified. Instead, token introspection should return current rev_seq when minted; clients should not be trusted to assert rev state.

kim: operational plan: 1) add rev_seq to revocation store (DB migration) 2) implement signed delta publish on revoke/restore 3) streaming gRPC push to Hosted edges + signed snapshot artifact for Private 4) proof endpoint and validator fallback 5) linter to flag code that trusts client-provided rev fields.

sam: timeline? we need this prioritized. I'll mark P0 for security-sensitive customers. Rough estimates: db migration + delta signers 2w, gRPC push + consumer in hosted edges 3w, proof endpoint + validator fallback 1w, private artifact workflow 2w. Total ~6w with parallel work.

jordyn: also add observability: rev_propagation_lag histogram, rev_proof_calls_total, rev_mismatch_alerts. Create ticket AUTH-4600.

infra-bot: security-scan: detected 9 services making naive token.rev_seq trust checks. https://ci.internal/scan/4387659876

kim: action items: sam -> triage customer impact + mitigation (short-term reduce TTL to 10s for critical routes), jordyn -> design doc & signing spec, lee -> implement proof endpoint & validator fallback, infra -> enable streaming in hosted and create artifact signer for Private.
sam: mitigation: set temporary runtime flag to reduce cache TTL to 10s for orgs that reported issues. We'll coordinate with ops. Also add instant blacklist check in edge auth path to call central revocation index for keys flagged critical.

jordyn: note about replay windows: some clients use cached tokens for longer than TTL; we need to ensure auditors can reconstruct that a revoked key was accepted by which node using signed deltas and receipts. Deltas should include origin timestamp and node ack logs should include delta_seq applied.

lee: security: protect proof endpoint from amplification. Rate-limit per-node and require mTLS between edges and control plane. Public-facing edges still call proof endpoint inside infra; never expose to user networks.

kim: communication plan: we'll post a migration RFC + security bulletin. For Private customers include artifact pull instructions and HSM signing recommendation.
sam: thanks all. cc @support @acct-eng when we have mitigation script. I'll open ticket AUTH-4600 and start the customer postmortem notes.
